solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detectives starting to bend and break up

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is kept

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors, police detectives
the opening letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police officers begin to bend the rules and then a gang is broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, short for Detective Inspector, is a standard crossword way to clue detectives; the plural gives DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To disband a group is to break it up so that its members separate and it stops existing as a unit.

clue.text: Degenerate put off current lecture

blocks.note: to deter someone is to put them off
I is the symbol for electric current
to orate is to lecture or speechify

explanation.surface: A sour description of someone dismissed as a degenerate who skipped a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' reads as a noun or adjective for a person, but here it is the verb. I for current comes from physics formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to degenerate is to decline in quality or condition, which is exactly what getting worse over time means.

clue.text: Rustled up dish

indicators.note: something whipped up is thrown together in a hurry, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all seven letters used

explanation.surface: Someone quickly made a dish from whatever was to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustled up' looks like one phrasal verb, but it splits: the first word is the fodder and the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A strudel is a layered pastry, often filled with apple, served as a dessert course, so it counts as a dish.

clue.text: Mark, in a part of the garden, shunned drink

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a flower bed is one part of a garden
a stain is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Someone stuck out in a corner of the garden, conspicuously refusing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A bed is the planted patch of a garden; 'Mark, in' reads as addressing a man called Mark, but it is the stain going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain deliberately, and in everyday use it especially means choosing not to take alcohol.

clue.text: Tyrant posted abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters are spread into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictator has been sent overseas, perhaps exiled or stationed in a foreign post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted abroad' reads as one diplomatic phrase, but 'abroad' only signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power who uses it cruelly, which is the core meaning of tyrant.

clue.text: Look — live part of brain

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or behold
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A neurologist pointing at a living brain region on a scan.
explanation.walkthrough: LO, as in 'lo and behold', is a common crossword stand-in for look.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is divided into large regions such as the frontal and temporal lobes, so a lobe is one of its parts.

clue.text: Garland made from tips of leafy evergreen initially

indicators.note: the tip of a word is taken to be its front end, so only opening letters count

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: A wreath woven from the green leaves of an evergreen plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a second signal, but it is itself one of the three words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is the Hawaiian flower garland hung around the neck as a welcome, so it is a kind of garland.

clue.text: Pancake left in rubbish container on island

indicators.note: something put in a receptacle ends up surrounded by it

blocks.note: a bin holds rubbish
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A pancake thrown away in a bin on some island.
explanation.walkthrough: B(L)IN, then I added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes, usually served with soured cream and caviar; the word is used here for a single one.

clue.text: Names school divisions

blocks.note: first meaning: words or labels used for things
second meaning: the periods into which a school year is split

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a register listing pupils by class, but the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both labels given to things and the blocks of the academic year, such as the spring and autumn periods.

clue.text: Tears around with Italian’s drinks

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: rips are tears in fabric
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about tearfully while an Italian's cocktails are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' wants to be crying, and 'tears around' to mean dashing about; it is rips, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are distilled alcoholic drinks such as gin, whisky and vodka, a broad category of beverage.

clue.text: Repent day after rage

indicators.note: coming after something means placed behind it, setting the order of the pieces

blocks.note: to seethe is to rage inwardly
daylight; day is the light part of the twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry the morning after a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives day first, but 'after' puts it behind rage in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the light is an idiom for realising one's errors and changing one's ways, often in a religious conversion.

clue.text: Friend’s regularly embarrassed

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A pal who keeps getting flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An embarrassed person blushes, turning that colour in the face, so the colour word stands for the feeling.

clue.text: A wish to meet team close by

indicators.note: things that meet join up end to end, so one piece follows directly on

blocks.note: taken as written
to long for something is to wish for it
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A fan hopes to meet their team when it is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wish' looks like a noun after 'A', but it stands for the verb long.
explanation.definitionFit: Something positioned alongside is next to or beside another thing, which means nearby or adjacent.

clue.text: Gossip given pear that’s been pureed

indicators.note: pureed food has been mashed to a pulp, so the letters are broken up and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone chattering while being handed some mashed pear, like baby food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder along with pear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something 'on the grapevine' means learning it through informal rumour, so the word names the gossip network.

clue.text: Greedily eying flipping game fish

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: Go is the Japanese board game
a ling is a long sea fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: An angler eyes up a sporting catch, greedy for a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game fish' reads as one phrase, as in angling, but splits into the game and the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone or something with obvious greedy or lustful interest.

clue.text: Fight most heartlessly with husband for affection

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is removed and only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: a war is a fight
the first and last letters of the word
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A couple bickering cruelly when what they want from each other is love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the husband on to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth in a person is friendliness and tenderness, the emotional sense of affection.

clue.text: Deliverer in food hall with one nacho regularly missing

indicators.note: letters missing at regular intervals leave every other one behind

blocks.note: a mess is a dining hall, as in the army
I is the Roman numeral for one
the second and fourth letters remain

explanation.surface: A delivery driver in a food court whose order is one nacho short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliverer' suggests a courier, and 'food hall' a shopping-centre food court; a mess is where soldiers eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A messiah is a saviour or liberator, someone who delivers people from oppression or sin.

clue.text: For example study love turning tense

indicators.note: turning round faces the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: e.g. is short for for example
a den is a private study
love is zero in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A student studying how love can turn into nervousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' tempts a grammar reading after 'turning', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being nervous, jumpy and unable to relax, which is what tense means here.

clue.text: Plenty of hair coiled round into a twist?

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the twist is a 1960s dance
a bun is hair wound round into a knot

explanation.surface: A thick head of hair wound round and twisted into a style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' looks like part of the hairstyle, but it is the dance; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a large quantity, more than enough, which is what plenty means as a noun.

clue.text: Relative is vague missing last two characters

indicators.note: missing the final two characters means the end of the word is cut away

blocks.note: something vague is unclear

explanation.surface: Someone's relation is hazy, not quite remembering things.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AR from the end of the synonym leaves the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is the brother of a parent, a family member and so a relative.

clue.text: Note is almost exclusive

indicators.note: almost all of something means it falls just short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: sole rights are exclusive rights

explanation.surface: A memo that is nearly private, for limited eyes only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a written message; it is the musical note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sol, also spelt soh, is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale used in singing.

clue.text: Former partner called in high spirits

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to cite is to call or summon, as before a court

explanation.surface: An old flame phoned in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called in' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'in' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excited is full of eager enthusiasm and energy, which is the lively mood described by high spirits.

clue.text: Add up either way

indicators.note: reading either way means forwards or backwards gives the same result

blocks.note: the word reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: An arithmetic tip: a sum checks the same whichever direction you add it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alone gives the answer; the indicator just confirms it is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up a bill is an informal British way of saying to add the figures together.

clue.text: I confess on radio to mobster’s killing

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: to sing is criminal slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: A broadcast confession to a gangland murder.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing, in criminal slang, is to inform or confess, so 'I confess' becomes 'I sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is gangster slang for murdering them, so icing is a mobster's word for a killing.

clue.text: Band strike

blocks.note: first meaning: a strip worn round the waist
second meaning: to hit hard

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like musicians walking out, but the words are two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a strap of leather or fabric around the waist and a verb meaning to hit hard.

clue.text: European agreement with passionate breadth of vision

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
yes expresses agreement
hot can mean ardent or passionate

explanation.surface: A fervent pro-European deal praised as far-sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breadth of vision' sounds like political foresight, but it means range of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshot is the distance or range over which one can see, as in 'within eyeshot', the literal span of sight.
